findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:124-140 `sync_queue_merged_task` returns False when `not queue_enabled(work)`. The call site at line 1049 sits inside the `selected_mode == "coordinator"` branch, and a False result goes straight to `managed_candidate` and handoff. design.md narrows the behavior to the queue status, while the spec requirement text ("exact PR of the task branch is merged") is not limited to the queue.
findings.summary: The spec says finish reconciles whenever the exact PR of the task branch is merged. The implementation only detects a merged PR through the publication queue status, so a managed candidate whose queue is not enabled still falls through to developer handoff.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:1049 calls `sync_queue_merged_task`, which calls `sync_merged_task`. Lines 1060-1082 then call `queue_local_status` and `sync_merged_task` again for state "merged". design.md Risks lists only "One extra PR read per finish of a managed candidate".
findings.summary: For a merged queue PR, `sync_merged_task` and `local_status` now run in the early check and again in the existing queue block. The design only mentions one extra PR read, and the second `sync_merged_task` call relies on being idempotent after the first fast-forward.
